Test case: open_tracking SUBSCRIBED is accepted and maps to ALLOW
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send subscriptions.email = {"open_tracking": {"consent": "SUBSCRIBED"}}.
Expected result: 202 Accepted. The adapter resolves the value to ProfilePermissionOperationType.ALLOW.
Source of truth / notes: ClientTrackingConsentStatus merges both directions because /client is a single POST.

Test case: click_tracking UNSUBSCRIBED is accepted and maps to DENY
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send subscriptions.email = {"click_tracking": {"consent": "UNSUBSCRIBED"}}.
Expected result: 202 Accepted. The adapter resolves the value to ProfilePermissionOperationType.DENY.

Test case: Both tracking types in one request
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send open_tracking SUBSCRIBED and click_tracking UNSUBSCRIBED together.
Expected result: 202. Open resolves ALLOW, click resolves DENY; the two travel different code paths from here.
Source of truth / notes: ALLOW rides inside subscribe(); DENY goes through unsubscribe_v2().

Test case: Tracking consent without an email identifier is rejected
Preconditions: A request whose profile carries only a phone_number
Steps: Send either tracking key with no email attribute.
Expected result: 400, error code "invalid", detail "An email identifier is required for email tracking consent.", source pointer /data/attributes/profile/data/attributes/email. No subscription is published.
Source of truth / notes: validate_tracking_consent_requires_email. Tracking consent is keyed on email, so this must fail at the boundary.

Test case: An email block with no marketing and no tracking is rejected
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send subscriptions.email = {} (or with only unrelated keys).
Expected result: 400 with "email must specify at least one of 'marketing', 'open_tracking', or 'click_tracking'."
Source of truth / notes: validate_email_subscription_parameters.

Test case: An unrecognised consent value is rejected by the DTO
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send {"open_tracking": {"consent": "MAYBE"}}.
Expected result: 400 before any adapter code runs; never a 500.
Source of truth / notes: Matt's answer to the KeyError review note: the enum rejects unknown values before the operation map is read.

Test case: A marketing-only request is unchanged
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send subscriptions.email = {"marketing": {...}} with no tracking keys.
Expected result: Behaviour identical to before the stack: list membership and marketing consent only, no tracking permissions touched.
Source of truth / notes: REGRESSION GUARD - this is the overwhelming majority of real traffic.

Test case: A request with no subscription keys keeps implicit marketing opt-in
Preconditions: POST /client/subscriptions with a company_id and an email identifier
Steps: Send a back-in-stock style request with no subscriptions block at all.
Expected result: Legacy behaviour preserved: the consumer subscribes every channel that has an identifier.
Source of truth / notes: has_marketing defaults True when nothing was requested AND no tracking was requested.

Test case: Deprecated revisions still work
Preconditions: Older API revisions that go through convert_from_deprecated_dto / convert_from_deprecated_oct24_dto
Steps: Send requests on both deprecated revisions.
Expected result: Both convert into ClientProfileUpsertQueryWithSubscriptions and behave as before.
Source of truth / notes: #145726 swapped the DTO type in both converters.

Test case: OpenAPI spec generates with no breaking change
Preconditions: CI
Steps: Let the V3 API Check run.
Expected result: Spec generation succeeds and no breaking changes are reported.
Source of truth / notes: Already green on #145726.

Test case: ALLOW is passed into subscribe() rather than written separately
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used; sync fallback enabled for the company
Steps: Send open_tracking SUBSCRIBED.
Expected result: subscribe() receives an OpenTrackingConsentRequest in open_tracking_consent; no unsubscribe_v2 call is made.

Test case: DENY goes through unsubscribe_v2()
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Send click_tracking UNSUBSCRIBED.
Expected result: unsubscribe_v2 is called with an UnsubscribeDTO whose UnsubscribeRequest carries action CLICK_TRACKING_CONSENT and the email as identifier.
Source of truth / notes: ALLOW and DENY are asymmetric by design - they are different service calls.

Test case: A mixed request splits correctly
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Send open_tracking SUBSCRIBED and click_tracking UNSUBSCRIBED.
Expected result: subscribe() gets the open ALLOW plus the email-marketing channel map; unsubscribe_v2 gets only the click DENY.
Source of truth / notes: Jon Parise asked this be asserted on both halves; Matt confirmed the existing test does.

Test case: unsubscribe_v2 runs BEFORE subscribe
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Send a mixed ALLOW/DENY request and record call order.
Expected result: unsubscribe_v2 is invoked first, then subscribe.
Source of truth / notes: Deliberate ordering, and the opposite of the KMS consumer's order in #145870 - see FM-04.

Test case: Metadata carries subscribe_method and client IP
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Send a tracking request from a known IP.
Expected result: Open and click metadata both carry subscribe_method and ip_address.
Source of truth / notes: Was a Cursor Bugbot finding on #145743; fixed in 590802116f6.

Test case: No email in the submitted data skips tracking entirely
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Reach process_subscription_sync with no email in submitted_data.
Expected result: Neither a consent request nor an unsubscribe request is built; marketing processing is unaffected.
Source of truth / notes: Belt-and-braces behind AC-04, for internal callers that bypass the DTO.

Test case: The sync path is only reached when KMS is off or publishing throws
Preconditions: Both hot settings in their normal state
Steps: Send a tracking request with KMS enabled.
Expected result: process_subscription (KMS) is used; process_subscription_sync is not called.

Test case: Sync fallback disabled drops the work rather than writing it
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used; sync fallback hot setting OFF for the company
Steps: Send a tracking request.
Expected result: Nothing is written. A "DropSyncSubscription" log is emitted for the company.
Source of truth / notes: is_sync_subscribe_fallback_enabled.

Test case: The sync path has no rollout gate
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting disabled for the company (the default)
Steps: Send a tracking request that reaches the sync path.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR. The rollout filter lives in the KMS path only, so the sync path may write tracking permissions with the rollout off.
Source of truth / notes: OPEN ISSUE: Peter raised exactly this on #145743 and the thread is still unresolved. Matt's answer was merge-ordering, not a gate. Worth a decision now that #145765 has landed.

Test case: Operations are mapped onto the proto message
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send open SUBSCRIBED and click UNSUBSCRIBED.
Expected result: The published Subscription carries open_tracking_consent = TRACKING_CONSENT_OPERATION_ALLOW and click_tracking_consent = TRACKING_CONSENT_OPERATION_DENY.
Source of truth / notes: k-repo #69340 added the fields to the contract.

Test case: Fields are omitted when no tracking decision was made
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send a marketing-only request.
Expected result: Neither tracking field is set on the message.
Source of truth / notes: The fields are only assigned when not None.

Test case: An invalid operation raises rather than publishing
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path
Steps: Call process_subscription with an operation that is not ALLOW or DENY.
Expected result: ValueError: Tracking consent operations must be ALLOW or DENY. Nothing is published.
Source of truth / notes: _validate_tracking_operations; other ProfilePermissionOperationType members exist.

Test case: A tracking-only request publishes a tracking-only message
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send only click_tracking UNSUBSCRIBED, no marketing.
Expected result: One Subscription with subscribe_to_email False, subscribe_to_sms False and an empty subscription_type, carrying the tracking field.
Source of truth / notes: This is the shape the consumer recognises as is_tracking_only.

Test case: A tracking request with the rollout off publishes NOTHING
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting disabled for the company (the default)
Steps: Send a tracking-only request.
Expected result: No KMS message at all. Critically, the request must NOT fall back to a legacy marketing subscribe.
Source of truth / notes: The subtlest guard in the stack: tracking_consent_requested is captured BEFORE the rollout filter, so the has_marketing fallback stays suppressed. Without it, 'do not track me' would become a marketing opt-in.

Test case: Marketing plus tracking publishes a single message
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send marketing plus both tracking keys.
Expected result: One Subscription carrying both the marketing channels and the tracking fields.

Test case: Rollout off leaves marketing untouched
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting disabled for the company (the default)
Steps: Send marketing plus tracking.
Expected result: The marketing subscribe publishes exactly as before; only the tracking fields are dropped, with a log and a metric.
Source of truth / notes: REGRESSION GUARD for the rollout period.

Test case: A Shopify request with tracking publishes two messages
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company; a customer_access_token present
Steps: Send a Shopify request with a tracking decision.
Expected result: A ShopifySubscription for the marketing work, plus a second Subscription carrying only the tracking fields with every subscribe flag false.
Source of truth / notes: ShopifySubscription has no tracking fields. group_id stays required on the extra message but must not add list membership.

Test case: A Shopify request without tracking is unchanged
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; a customer_access_token present
Steps: Send a Shopify request with no tracking keys.
Expected result: Exactly one ShopifySubscription, as before the stack.
Source of truth / notes: REGRESSION GUARD. #145765 changed `return self._send_shopify_subscription(...)` to a bare call so a second message could follow.

Test case: The extra message does not add list membership
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; as SH-01
Steps: Publish and consume both messages; inspect list membership.
Expected result: The profile is on the list once, from the Shopify message only; the tracking-only message adds no membership.

Test case: Continue-with-Shop resume does not write a false refusal
Preconditions: A Shop form that redirects away and returns
Steps: Submit through the Shop path with marketing unchecked, then return.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR. Today the Shop path subscribes regardless of the unchecked marketing box.
Source of truth / notes: OPEN ISSUE: Peter's open question #1 on fender #70901. The stopgap gate avoids a false tracking refusal but the marketing side is unresolved; needs a tracked follow-up.

Test case: ALLOW writes a positive permission record
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Publish and consume a message with open_tracking_consent ALLOW.
Expected result: A ProfilePermission row for OPEN_TRACKING_CONSENT with permission_outcome true, customer_id and subject_id set to the profile.

Test case: DENY revokes through unsubscribe_v2
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a message with click_tracking_consent DENY.
Expected result: unsubscribe_v2 is called and the click permission ends in a refused state.

Test case: A tracking-only DENY does not call subscribe()
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a tracking-only DENY message (KP-04's shape).
Expected result: subscribe() is skipped entirely; only the revocation is applied. No list membership, no Subscribed to List event.
Source of truth / notes: is_tracking_only plus should_subscribe. Without this guard a refusal would subscribe the shopper.

Test case: A tracking-only ALLOW still calls subscribe()
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a tracking-only ALLOW message.
Expected result: subscribe() is called, because ALLOW is applied inside it, but no marketing channels are subscribed.
Source of truth / notes: has_tracking_allow is why should_subscribe is not simply 'not is_tracking_only'.

Test case: Marketing plus tracking applies both
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a message carrying marketing channels and both tracking fields.
Expected result: List membership and marketing consent are written, and both tracking permissions are recorded.

Test case: A message with no email drops the tracking decision
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a tracking message whose submitted_data has no email.
Expected result: The tracking work is skipped with a "SubscriptionExecutor.TrackingConsentDrop" log and the _no_email metric. Marketing processing is unaffected.

Test case: Messages without tracking fields behave exactly as before
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a message published before the rollout, with no tracking fields.
Expected result: Identical behaviour to current production.
Source of truth / notes: REGRESSION GUARD - every in-flight message at deploy time looks like this.

Test case: A company_id mismatch drops the message
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume a message whose company_id does not match the list's company.
Expected result: The message is dropped without writing anything.
Source of truth / notes: Pre-existing guard; confirm tracking did not bypass it.

Test case: The Shopify consumer is unaffected
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Consume ShopifySubscription messages.
Expected result: No behaviour change; the Shopify consumer never sees tracking fields.

Test case: All four settings default to off
Preconditions: A company that was never added to the rollout
Steps: Read get_global, get_allow_list, get_percentage and is_enabled_for_company.
Expected result: False, empty, 0, and False respectively.
Source of truth / notes: CompanyRolloutHotSettingBundle generates _global_setting, _allow_list, _disallow_list and _percentage_cutoff.

Test case: An allow-listed company is included
Preconditions: enable_for_company(<id>) applied
Steps: Send a tracking request for that company and for another.
Expected result: Tracking is honoured for the allow-listed company and dropped for the other.
Source of truth / notes: This is how internal test accounts should be enabled - not the global flag.

Test case: The disallow list overrides allow-list and percentage
Preconditions: A company both allow-listed and disallowed
Steps: Send a tracking request.
Expected result: Tracking is dropped. The disallow list wins.
Source of truth / notes: Useful as a per-company kill switch during rollout.

Test case: Percentage rollout includes the expected share
Preconditions: change_percentage(10)
Steps: Evaluate is_enabled_for_company across a sample of ids.
Expected result: Roughly ten percent included, and stable per company across calls.

Test case: Dropping emits a metric and a log
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting disabled for the company (the default)
Steps: Send a tracking request and watch metrics.
Expected result: forms.client_subscription_tracking_consent_drop_rollout_disabled increments and a "ClientSubscription.TrackingConsentDrop" log is written.
Source of truth / notes: The signal that tells you whether anyone is sending before rollout.

Test case: Permission rows carry the right identity
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Apply an ALLOW and inspect ProfilePermission.
Expected result: action matches OPEN_TRACKING_CONSENT or CLICK_TRACKING_CONSENT, identifier is the email, customer_id and subject_id are the profile id, permission_outcome reflects ALLOW or DENY.

Test case: Tracking consent appears on the profile export
Preconditions: A profile with both tracking permissions recorded
Steps: Export the profile and inspect the consent keys.
Expected result: email_open_tracking_consent and email_click_tracking_consent appear with their _timestamp counterparts.
Source of truth / notes: Keys come from consent_property_key(channel, communication_type).

Test case: A never-consented profile exports nothing for tracking
Preconditions: A profile with no tracking permission rows
Steps: Export the profile.
Expected result: No tracking consent keys are emitted; a NEVER_SUBSCRIBED state is not exported as a refusal.
Source of truth / notes: Absence of consent is not a denial - do not let it read as one.

Test case: ALLOW then DENY then ALLOW ends in the right state
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send the three requests in sequence for one email.
Expected result: The final state is ALLOW with a timestamp from the last request. No interleaving leaves a stale outcome.
Source of truth / notes: The sequence a real shopper can produce by resubmitting a form.

Test case: Marketing consent is never inferred from a tracking decision
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send tracking-only ALLOW and tracking-only DENY requests.
Expected result: Email marketing consent is unchanged in both cases.
Source of truth / notes: FORMS-34863's acceptance criterion: tracking-only requests change only tracking permissions.

Test case: Renderer-private choice tokens never reach a permission or property
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Submit a real consent block and inspect every written row, property and event.
Expected result: The strings MARKETING, TRACKING and COMBINED appear nowhere. Only ALLOW/DENY per tracking type is stored.
Source of truth / notes: Explicit contract in fender's marketingTrackingConsent.ts; this is the backend half of that promise.

Test case: A retryable unsubscribe failure retries the whole message
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Make unsubscribe_v2 raise a retryable exception during consumption.
Expected result: The message is retried through attempt_retry.

Test case: A non-retryable unsubscribe failure DROPS the revocation
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Make unsubscribe_v2 raise a non-retryable exception.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR. Today: a metric, a log, and the message is dropped - no retry, no dead-letter. A consent revocation is lost.
Source of truth / notes: OPEN ISSUE, compliance-sensitive. Peter raised it on #145870 and none of the three proposed fixes addresses it. Needs an explicit contract with SCM / email-platforms before rollout.

Test case: A retry does not double-subscribe
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Force a retryable unsubscribe failure AFTER subscribe() has already succeeded.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR. The consumer calls subscribe() first, so a retry re-runs it and emits a second Subscribed to List.
Source of truth / notes: OPEN ISSUE. subscribe() is deliberately NOT idempotent at the event layer - subscribe_processor.py notes flows and webhooks rely on the event firing even for an existing member - so a duplicate can re-trigger a welcome flow.

Test case: Consumer and sync paths order the two calls the same way
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Compare call order in the consumer against process_subscription_sync.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE DIVERGENCE. The sync path calls unsubscribe first; the consumer calls subscribe first.
Source of truth / notes: Relevant to the #145870 decision: Matt's option 2 (move unsubscribe above subscribe) would make the consumer match what the sync path already does.

Test case: A partially applied mixed request is recoverable
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Make subscribe() fail after unsubscribe_v2 succeeded, then retry the request.
Expected result: Re-running produces the intended end state. Matt's argument is that a request never holds ALLOW and DENY for the same permission, so the retry is safe.
Source of truth / notes: Peter's atomicity question on #145743; thread resolved, but worth a test that pins the claim.

Test case: A KMS publish failure carries tracking into the fallback
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch off, so KMS is the publish path; sync fallback enabled
Steps: Make the KMS publish raise.
Expected result: The sync fallback runs and receives the same tracking operations.
Source of truth / notes: Both call sites of _attempt_sync_subscription_based_on_hotsetting pass them.

Test case: Request-building logic agrees across both paths
Preconditions: Both paths exercised with identical input
Steps: Compare the requests built by the sync adapter against build_tracking_consent_requests.
Expected result: Identical ALLOW requests and DENY unsubscribe requests.
Source of truth / notes: #145870 adds the shared builder but does NOT refactor #145743's inline copy, so two code paths must stay in step. Flag on review.

Test case: DENY is written before the bot and abuse checks run
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used; FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send a tracking DENY from a request the protections would flag.
Expected result: DOCUMENT THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR. unsubscribe_v2 runs before subscribe(), and the protections live inside subscribe(), so the DENY lands while the ALLOW is dropped.
Source of truth / notes: OPEN ISSUE. Raised by Rohit on #145743; Matt asked Jon Parise whether is_suspicious_request / _is_subscription_request_blocked / rate limiting should mirror onto unsubscribe_v2. Jon approved the PR but never answered that thread.

Test case: A third party cannot flip tracking for an arbitrary email
Preconditions: FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Craft a request with a known company_id and someone else's email.
Expected result: ASSESS AND RECORD. Matt's position: the impact is bounded - marketing consent is untouched and it moves in the privacy-safe direction - and the bot checks are heuristics, not identity.
Source of truth / notes: Decide whether this is accepted risk before the rollout widens. It is a public client endpoint.

Test case: Rate limiting applies to tracking-only requests
Preconditions: FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting enabled for the company
Steps: Send tracking-only requests above the endpoint's rate limit.
Expected result: The limiter engages as it does for marketing subscribes.
Source of truth / notes: Part of the same question to Jon.

Test case: Rollout drops are visible
Preconditions: FormsMarketingTrackingConsentHotSetting disabled for the company (the default)
Steps: Send tracking requests and watch the dashboard.
Expected result: forms.client_subscription_tracking_consent_drop_rollout_disabled increments. A non-zero rate before rollout means someone is already sending.
Source of truth / notes: Dashboards are linked in the #145743 / #145765 / #145870 PR descriptions.

Test case: Consumer drops are visible and distinguishable
Preconditions: #145870 merged, so the KMS consumer applies tracking fields
Steps: Trigger a no-email drop and an unsubscribe-error drop.
Expected result: The _no_email counter and the error counter move independently, so a compliance-relevant drop is not hidden among benign ones.
Source of truth / notes: The unsubscribe-error counter is the alarm for FM-02. It should be alerted on, not just graphed.

Test case: Sync fallback usage is visible
Preconditions: KMSSubscribeKillSwitch ON, so the synchronous path is used
Steps: Force the fallback.
Expected result: SyncSubscription log and the forms sync-subscribe metric both fire.
Source of truth / notes: Matters because the sync path is the ungated one - see SY-09.

Test case: Canary on an ondemand before widening the rollout
Preconditions: #145870 merged; an ondemand instance running the KMS consumer
Steps: Run the consumer against real traffic for one allow-listed company and watch the drop and error counters.
Expected result: Tracking permissions appear for real submissions, with no unexplained drops.
Source of truth / notes: Per the smoke-test-plan skill; the consumer is an async workload so a soak is the right check.
